name: Raffles Medical
summary: Islandwide clinic network many expats use for GP, health screening, paediatric panels, and first-stop private care — confirm mental-health and dental carve-outs separately.
body: Raffles Medical clinics are a common first GP relationship for newcomers who want English-first private care and islandwide coverage. Before you attach, confirm your employer insurer’s panel list, nearest clinic hours to home and office, and what to do after 10pm — clinic networks are not a substitute for knowing your closest appropriate A&E. Families often use the network for paediatric acute visits when panel rates apply; still keep a named paediatrician relationship if you want continuity. For elective hospital admissions, ask HR for the Letter of Guarantee workflow early — foreigners without MediSave commonly face large admission deposits without an LOG. Mental-health outpatient (psychology / counselling) and dental are frequently excluded or capped on basic corporate riders — ask HR for the benefits schedule before you assume sessions or scaling are reimbursable. Fertility investigations may start at a GP panel, but MOH ART co-funding is citizenship-gated at public AR centres — EP–EP couples should budget cash rates and not assume MediSave. If you arrived with controlled ADHD / anxiety meds under HSA approval, book a GP or specialist early so your local prescription path is ready before the import supply ends. Pair with the healthcare, dental, personal-medication, paediatrician, newborn-pass, IVF, and mental-health guides for triage.
